subject: Air-gapped Observability: evidence-bundle & SIEM handoff proposal
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Air-gapped Observability: evidence-bundle & SIEM handoff proposal

Hi Alan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion I sketched an approach for how Redwood can deliver observability artifacts from an on-prem / VPC (no-egress) deployment to Acme's SIEM without creating a persistent outbound tunnel from your production network. The attached PDF is a short spec; main points below: 

- Evidence-bundle model: Redwood creates time-windowed bundles (e.g., 1h) containing redacted LDJSON syslog, aggregated metrics snapshots (Prometheus text format), and compressed span traces (OTLP JSON). Bundles are signed with our artifact key and hashed.
- Local sanitization/scrubbing pipeline: configurable scrub rules at the agent-level to mask PII before bundle write. We recommend default field-level masks + allowlist for debug fields.
- Transport options (customer choice):
  1) Pull-by-customer agent: customer-run collector pulls signed bundles from a secured internal endpoint (no outbound egress required by Redwood).
  2) Air-gap transfer: bundle written to removable media or secure intermediary (SFTP jump host) which Acme transfers to your central SIEM ingestion pipeline.
  3) Brokered push-from-DMZ: when allowed, a dedicated transfer appliance in DMZ does an authenticated push to your Splunk HEC endpoint using mutual TLS.
- Integrity & audit: each bundle includes a manifest, SHA256 checksums, timestamped signature, and a short provenance file mapping model versions + config (for audit).
- Tracing hooks & sampling: We include trace context extraction and can strip payloads, retain span metadata, and apply deterministic sampling to reduce volume but preserve SLO regression observability.
- Retention & automatic expiry: bundles are ephemeral with TTLs and auto-delete policy; we can provide a verifiable delete log for audits.

Open questions for your security team: allowed transfer modes, retention max, and whether Acme wants Redwood to include raw stack traces (we recommend NOT by default).

Attaching: evidence-bundle-spec.pdf (short spec), sample-syslog.ldjson, splunk-hec-config.txt (example HEC mapping for when push is allowed).

Next steps: If this approach looks aligned, we propose a short proof-of-concept: deliver a 24-hour bundle from a staging private deployment, hand it to your SIEM team for ingestion, and walk through the verification steps.

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@acmebank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped Observability: evidence-bundle & SIEM handoff proposal

Soojin —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few clarifying points from our security and compliance reviewers: 

1) No persistent outbound allowed: our prod networks cannot have long-lived egress. Option (1) pull-by-customer or (2) air-gap transfer are acceptable.
2) Data classification: any log fields with PAN / SSN / account identifiers must be redacted before leaving the host.
3) Verifiable deletion: we need evidence that bundles are removed from your systems after transfer and an integrity log with checksums.

Questions:
- If we choose the pull-by-customer option, what auth mechanism do you support for the internal endpoint? (mTLS, API key, signed URL?)
- For the air-gap transfer, can the bundle manifest include a short statement of which scrub rules ran (hash of the scrub config) so our auditors can verify the applied policy?

If you can answer these, I'll route to procurement and our infosec contacts for a brief review.

— Alan
Alan Cho
Head of InfoSec Engineering, Acme Bank
alan.cho@acmebank.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@acmebank.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Sep 2028 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped Observability: evidence-bundle & SIEM handoff proposal

Thanks Alan — good constraints, and agreed on redaction-first. Quick answers and implementation notes: 

- Auth for pull-endpoint: we support customer-initiated mTLS (preferred) and signed short-lived URLs using our artifact signing service. For pull, we expose an internal-only endpoint inside the customer's VPC tied to a certificate thumbprint; the client (your collector) will need to present the matching client cert to download.
- Manifest: yes — the manifest will include a scrub-config-hash (SHA256) that is itself signed by Redwood. That gives you an immutable pointer to the exact scrub rules applied.
- Verifiable deletion: we produce a deletion record (signed timestamped ledger entry) and a periodic digest that you can reconcile. We also log the bundle lifecycle as part of the audit trail we ship with the bundle.

Implementation detail: to reduce friction we recommend building a small customer collector (we can provide a reference Go binary) that runs as a scheduled job inside your restricted network. It supports mTLS and can ingest bundles into Splunk by calling a local forwarder or staging HEC behind the DMZ. For strictly air-gapped customers, the collector can export to an encrypted USB key and verify checksum after copy.

Irene and Monica — assigning to you to review the promised scrub rule defaults and the collector reference implementation. Alan — happy to put this in a short SOW for the proof-of-concept.

- Marcus
Principal Engineer, Production Runtime
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Priya Sharma <psharma@splunkpartners.io>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@acmebank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Sep 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped Observability: evidence-bundle & SIEM handoff proposal

Hi all — Priya from Splunk Partner Engineering. Quick notes from the Splunk ingestion side: 

- For no-egress environments, the forwarder-to-broker pattern works well: you run a heavy forwarder inside the network to collect bundles and write to a broker VM (staging HEC or intermediate indexing node) that your SIEM ops team operates. The forwarder can validate the bundle signature and run local transforms.
- If you allow a transfer appliance in the DMZ, HEC over mTLS is easiest for structured metrics and events. We'll provide hardened forwarder images that have the bundle verifier built-in and a configuration that maps Redwood artifacts to Splunk sourcetypes.
- We can also provide a deterministic ingestion playbook for auditors showing how the scrub-config-hash maps to field transformations applied in ingestion.

Attaching: hardened-forwarder-readme.txt (we sent a copy to Marcus offline).

If useful, we can set up a 30m runbook session with your SIEM ops to validate the sample-syslog.ldjson ingestion.

— Priya
Partner Engineer, Splunk Partners
psharma@splunkpartners.io

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@acmebank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Sep 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped Observability: evidence-bundle & SIEM handoff proposal

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps: 

1) Acme preference: pull-by-customer (mTLS) + optional air-gap transfer for high-sensitivity artifacts.
2) Redwood actions (owner):
   - Marcus: finalize reference collector (mTLS + signed URL fallback) — target: 2028-09-14.
   - Irene: produce scrub-rule defaults and mapping doc (include scrub-config-hash) — target: 2028-09-12.
   - Monica: prepare 24h PoC bundle from staging private deploy and package audit ledger — target: 2028-09-13.
3) Alan / Acme actions: share cert thumbprint and a contact for SIEM ops. Alan to confirm acceptable retention window and whether raw stack traces may be included for debug (we recommend they be excluded).
4) Redwood will open RED-4821 (PoC work) and share runbook + Drive folder (link below).

I've attached the evidence-bundle-spec.pdf and a small sample (sample-syslog.ldjson) for your SIEM team to try ingesting. Marcus will follow up with the collector binary and deployment notes.

If nobody objects, I'll convert this thread into a formal SOW outline and add the tasks to RED-4821.

Best,

— Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
